objective: Increase the expected Geometry/Construction and Weathering/Context portions of the 100-point Visual Fidelity Gate by replacing the apartment facade's single slab-like window-sill/drip fallback with a manufactured, physically drained aluminum sill assembly, while keeping visual scoring locked until actual native-4K evidence exists.
priorityRationale: The existing HD_WindowSillDrip was one rectangular aluminum block under each of 30 facade windows. In frontal/oblique/grazing benchmark views this can read as a primitive ledge rather than a manufactured sliding-sash lower-frame interface. Because visible primitive-placeholder geometry is a critical automatic FAIL and the lower-frame interface influences contact shadow, runoff logic, metal highlights and temporal silhouette stability, this was higher-value than adding unrelated decoration.

commitsBeforeRunRecord.message: qa: define facade sill drainage construction contract
docs: add facade sill drainage lookdev
feat: build physical facade sill drainage assemblies

components: three-piece exterior skirt creating two true drainage openings
existing lower sash frame retained as a separate assembly
constructionReasoning.dimensionClaimBoundary: These dimensions are conservative benchmark reconstruction assumptions. They are not claimed as the dimensions of an identified historical commercial sash model.
constructionReasoning.mountingInterfaces: The generated tray is seated into the existing lower sash-frame interface rather than floating below it. Its front edge sits behind the segmented exterior skirt so each 50 mm interruption exposes a real recessed drainage path. The drip nose projects farther outward than the skirt. Only the 30 legacy HD_WindowSillDrip renderers are disabled; other existing sash/glass/gasket/latch components remain independent.
constructionReasoning.orientationExposure: Exterior is +Z. Upward tray surfaces are rain/sun exposed; the skirt and nose are rain/sun exposed. Drain recesses are intended to read darker from geometry/occlusion rather than painted darkness. Dry benchmark wetness remains zero.
constructionReasoning.geometryVsMaterial: Tray fall, 20 mm section thickness, segmented skirt, 50 mm drainage gaps, recess depth and drip-nose projection are geometry. Fine anodized/extrusion microstructure, oxide response and micro-scratches remain material detail. No illumination is baked into albedo.
constructionReasoning.weatheringCausality: RainLedge + DrainRunoff + UVExposure are attached to appropriate sill renderers. Aluminum itself receives no ferrous-rust source. Current wetness is zero.

materialPolicy.workflow: Unity Standard metallic workflow with canonical generated microstructure maps when present
materialPolicy.albedo: approximately float RGB 0.55/0.57/0.56 before lighting; no painted highlight
materialPolicy.microstructure: fine anisotropy-like extrusion-oriented grain plus irregularity; metric UVs are cut into eight deterministic phase bins
materialPolicy.angularResponse: Metallic Fresnel/grazing response must arise from the Standard BRDF plus the coherent reflection environment; emission and painted rim/highlight energy are rejected.

lodImplementation.topologyPolicy: LOD1/2/3 consolidate the same tray + three skirt segments + drip-nose topology into a single mesh. The two physical drainage openings are intentionally preserved through LOD3 instead of collapsing to a slab.

reflectionEvidenceBinding: No sill-specific reflection-probe mutation is performed during a probe request. The established reflection render-state fingerprint already hashes every active renderer identity/hierarchy, transform, mesh state, material state, texture state and scene dependency. Once this generated root exists in the persisted candidate, any sill geometry/material/render-state drift across reflection request/poll/completion/pre-still invalidates the shared fingerprint. This is evidence coherence only and is not a visual-quality claim.

functionalBasis: YKK AP technical watertightness guidance documents lower-frame water-head / pressure-equalized sash water-management concepts and emphasizes water-tight frame/body interfaces.
LIXIL PRESEA-H documentation confirms RC-frame sliding-window systems with explicit water-tightness performance and aluminum exterior sash construction context.
sourceResearch.claimLimit: The sources support the functional need for a real lower-frame water-management path and interfaces. They do not establish the exact benchmark dimensions used here.

unresolvedRenderedRisks: The custom tray cross-section currently has hard recalculated profile edges rather than an explicit millimetric edge roll. If the recessed tray edge still catches an implausibly razor-thin grazing highlight, add physical bevel geometry instead of compensating in the material.
The assumed 8 mm lower-frame seating must be checked in actual oblique pixels for both visible gaps and interpenetration with existing sash/gasket geometry.
The 50 mm drainage openings may be too visually large or too weak at the benchmark distance; only actual native-4K evidence can establish the right apparent scale.
Thirty product-identical sill assemblies are correct as manufactured repetition, but eight UV phase bins may still leave obvious synchronized appearance across the facade.
Anodized-aluminum highlight width and recess darkness must be checked under the actual midsummer sun/sky/reflection state; no source-side rule can prove filmic response.
LOD0 five-renderer to consolidated LOD1/2/3 transitions preserve geometry in source, but actual animated-crossfade dither/shimmer or highlight centroid movement remains unverified.
Unity 6000.3.0f1 compile and Editor callback behavior remain unverified because no Unity runner has executed this branch.
